Step: Classify input using structured questions routed to the Laya-AI service.

A non-streaming, single-forward-pass step that sends questions to the
`laya-serve` HTTP service. Each question has a type (choice, score, or NouL)
and criteria that define the acceptable answer space.

Step: Declarative tabular data manipulation.

Applies a pipeline of operations (filter, sort, aggregate, join, etc.) to a
JSON array of rows and returns JSON.

FanOutStep.description:
Step: Fan out over a dynamic runtime array with concurrent branch execution.

Takes an array produced at runtime (e.g., from a Generate step) and processes
each item concurrently through branch workflows, with optional grouping support.

item_var.description: Variable name for the current item in branch context (default: "item").

max_concurrency.description: Optional lower-only branch concurrency; None inherits the run cap (default four).

name.description: Optional name for the combined output (referenced by later steps as {{name}}).

path.description: Optional JSON path into the source value to extract the array.

source.description: Source of the array (named output, "last", or "input"). Supports template variables.

oneOf.description: One branch per item, all using the same template workflow.
Group items by a key field and route each group to a different branch workflow.

Group items by a tags field (array of strings) and run matching branches for each tag.
An item can produce multiple branches if it has multiple matching tags.

inline_tools.description:
Inline tool definitions — built-in tools configured directly on the step.
These are synthesized into ToolRows at execution time (no DB lookup).
Explicit Gate tools retain durable clarification; resumed final output still validates.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retry attempts if JSON parsing/validation fails (default 0).

memory.description: Explicit opt-in to use conversation memory for this step (default off).

schema.description:
Optional JSON Schema Draft 7 subset; absence permits any complete JSON value.
Supports boolean schemas, type (including unions), enum/const, nested properties,
required, schema/boolean additionalProperties and items, numeric bounds/multipleOf,
string length and collection size bounds, and descriptive annotations.
Schema admission rejects unknown keywords, references, regex/format, combinators,
tuples and uniqueItems. Limits: 64 KiB JSON, depth 32, 4096 JSON nodes, 256 subschemas.
Compiled before provider work; every complete response is validated before publication.

RulesetStep.description:
Step: Evaluate business rulesets against the current workflow context.

Each ruleset is evaluated in priority order. When a ruleset's condition matches
the current context, its effects are applied. Effects include:
- `set` — set a context value (variable/named_output)
- `append_reason` — append a reason string to the step output
- `set_output` — set a value in the step's JSON output

Rule decisions are captured in the step trace for auditability.

The supervisor agent only gets agent-tools (no DB tools) — clean separation
of planner vs executor. It dynamically decides which agents to call and when
the task is complete.

Workflow.description:

A workflow is a sequence of steps that can include prompt calls, mapping, routing,
and parallel branches.
